title: Opening, ten years of recordings, changing music business
summary: Monk Rowe opens the interview; Monheit discusses her first CD in 2000, steady output, and how the business keeps changing.

Vocalist Jane Monheit was born in Oakdale, NY on November 3, 1977. She graduated from the Manhattan School of Music and was a finalist in the 1998 Thelonious Monk Jazz Institute vocal competition. Her most recent recording is “Home” on the Emarcy/Universal label.
Jane was interviewed in Clinton, NY, on August 20, 2010, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
My name is Monk Rowe, off camera, and we are at Hamilton College. I’m very pleased to have Jane Monheit as my guest for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive.
I’ve been looking forward to talking to you, and I’ve been sort of following your career because I know your husband and your father-in-law quite well.
It’s been about ten years since your first CD? Is that right?
Yeah. It came out in May of 2000 my first record, so yeah, it’s been ten years.
And I was looking at your list and it’s pretty consistent. You have about a CD almost every year.

Yeah, yeah. There’ve been a couple of longer breaks, a year and a half or so here and there, depending on what’s going on during times when there was intense touring and stuff like that you know. There was a longer space between “Surrender” and the “Lovers and Dreamers and Me” because I had a baby.

Well I had it while we were making “Lovers and Dreamers and Me.” It — him. But yeah, it depends. It’s been eight studio albums and two DVDs in ten years, and two “best of” records which is totally weird at 32, I mean two “best of’s” at 32.

Yeah. Now was that your — I want to spend a little time seeing if I can get a handle on how the music business works these days — not that I ever really knew. But I get a lot of students asking me now, and I don’t really know.
It changes constantly. No one’s got a real handle on it now. If they did the record companies would be in better shape.
